doc.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021

chapter: Bay Area youth and early listening
title: Crystal radio, the Beatles, Hendrix and playing electric bass in high school
summary: He listened to all kinds of music on a crystal radio, saw the Beatles and Hendrix live, and played funk and rock on electric bass outside school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: So hearing that just blew my mind you know. I didn’t know what they were doing but it went boing — you know something big. And so it had my heart, from that age. But then in high school I heard James Brown and I used to have a little crystal radio set. I don’t know if you know what that is, but you —

Well then you know you don’t have batteries, we had a wire strung between two trees in the backyard and I had these little earphones. And I’ve always been a night person. So I’d lay in bed and listen, I’d just turn this little dial of whatever station would come up. I’d listen to all kinds of music, you know, Gospel music, like black Gospel music, and jazz and blues and country music you know like the Appalachian kind. What’s the name for that?
Yeah, bluegrass though, I mean some of them fiddle players and guitar players playing, you know?
You’re right. I remember Ed Shaughnessy talking about that, he said that stuff swings also.
Yeah, I used to watch Hee Haw sometimes. And they had a guitar player on there and a fiddle player that was mean. And you know then I heard the Beatles in person in San Francisco.
You were at the last Beatles concert?
Not the last. One of the first waves.

’64 I think it was or something like that. I heard them and I heard Jimi Hendrix live. And I used to play electric bass in a band and we’d do this in high school. I played trombone at school in the jazz band and all that, but outside of school I played electric bass and we played funk and rock and we had our own little songs we wrote. You know we played some James Brown and one or two Beatles tunes, but you know whatever tunes — and we used to play for the school dances around the area.
